newsitem.title: ZAIRE: First refugees arrive from empty Zaire camp.
newsitem.headline: First refugees arrive from empty Zaire camp.

text.p: Small numbers of Rwandan Hutu refugees arrived near the northeastern Zairean city of Kisangani on Friday, saying they had walked for three days since their camp was attacked.

A group of 13 refugees was the first to emerge from Kasese Camp, 25 km (15 miles) south of Kisangani, which had 55,000 refugees last week but was emptied by the time Tutsi-dominated rebels allowed a U.N. mission to reach the camp on Thursday.
The Hutu refugees including three unaccompanied children said they fled Kasese when they heard gunshots and screaming.

"On Tuesday morning I heard screaming and shooting. I ran into the forest away from the firing...Everyone panicked. People were running left and right and families were separated," Papa-Eve Ngendaimana told Reuters.
The refugees said in the confusion they did not see who attacked the camp and did not know if people had been killed.

Zairean villagers from Kasese have said hundreds of refugees were killed in the camp when it was attacked on Tuesday. The rebels say they intervened to stop an attack by local people but were ambushed by former Rwandan Hutu troops and militiamen.
"I want to go back to Rwanda," said refugee Efrazine Duosabimungu, from the Rwandan capital Kigali, adding she had been separated from her husband when she fled Kasese camp.

"We all scattered into the forest to escape gunfire. It carried on for a long time. I spent the night in the forest and it was hard because there was nothing to eat," said Duosabimungu, who had a one-year-old child with her.
A U.N. aerial survey on Friday confirmed another 30,000 Rwandan refugees had fled their camp at Biaro, 45 km (25 miles) south of Kisangani, which was captured by the rebels on March 15.
Aid agencies accused the Tutsi-dominated rebels of seeking a "final solution" to the refugees by condemning them to die.
